mcqs.learning_point: Understand conductivity of heat and electricity
mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the ability of metals and non‑metals to conduct heat and electricity?

options.A: Metals conduct both heat and electricity well, while non‑metals are poor conductors of both.
options.B: Metals conduct electricity well but heat poorly; non‑metals conduct heat well but electricity poorly.
options.C: Metals conduct heat well but electricity poorly; non‑metals conduct electricity well but heat poorly.
options.D: Both metals and non‑metals conduct heat and electricity equally well.

mcqs.answer: Metals conduct both heat and electricity well, while non‑metals are poor conductors of both.
mcqs.explanation: Metals have free electrons that allow efficient transfer of both thermal energy and electric charge, making them good conductors of heat and electricity. Non‑metals lack such free electrons, so they are generally poor conductors of both. Options B, C and D describe incorrect relationships.

mcqs.question: The property of sonority in metals is best described as:

options.A: Ability to be drawn into thin wires
options.B: Ability to produce a resonant sound when struck
options.C: Ability to reflect light giving a shiny appearance
options.D: Ability to be hammered into thin sheets

mcqs.answer: Ability to produce a resonant sound when struck
mcqs.explanation: Sonority refers to the characteristic ringing sound a metal makes when struck, due to its elastic nature. It is unrelated to ductility (A), lustre (C), or malleability (D).

mcqs.learning_point: Relate metallic properties to common uses
mcqs.question: Which property of metals makes them especially suitable for cooking utensils?
mcqs.explanation: Cooking utensils need to transfer heat quickly and evenly to food; metals with high thermal conductivity (e.g., copper, aluminium) fulfill this requirement. Sonority, brittleness, and low density are not relevant to this use.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a common metal encountered in everyday life?
mcqs.explanation: Iron is a widely used metal found in tools, construction, and household items. Sodium chloride, silica, and calcium carbonate are compounds, not elemental metals.

mcqs.question: Lustre in metals refers to:

options.B: The shiny appearance due to reflection of light
options.C: The capacity to be hammered into sheets
options.D: The tendency to produce sound when struck

mcqs.answer: The shiny appearance due to reflection of light
mcqs.explanation: Lustre is the characteristic shine of a metal surface caused by the reflection of light from its smooth, polished surface. Conductivity, malleability, and sonority are different properties.

mcqs.question: Which process best demonstrates the malleability of a metal?

options.A: Stretching a copper wire into a thin thread
options.B: Hammering a sheet of aluminium into a thin foil
options.C: Bending a steel rod without breaking

mcqs.answer: Hammering a sheet of aluminium into a thin foil
mcqs.explanation: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without breaking. Option B directly shows this. Stretching into a wire tests ductility, bending a rod tests toughness, and melting tests thermal properties.

mcqs.question: A metal that can be drawn into thin wires possesses which property?
mcqs.explanation: Ductility is the property that allows a metal to be stretched into thin wires or rods. Malleability relates to shaping into sheets, sonority to sound, and lustre to shine.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conductivity of heat and electricity
mcqs.question: A student places a metal spoon in a pot of boiling water and a wooden spoon in another identical pot. After five minutes, which spoon will be hotter and why?

options.A: The metal spoon, because metals conduct heat better than wood.
options.B: The wooden spoon, because wood is a better heat conductor than metal.
options.C: Both spoons will be at the same temperature because the water temperature is the same.
options.D: Neither spoon will become hot because heat transfer does not depend on the material of the spoon.

mcqs.answer: The metal spoon, because metals conduct heat better than wood.
mcqs.explanation: Metals have free electrons that transfer thermal energy rapidly, so the metal spoon quickly absorbs heat from the boiling water. Wood is a poor conductor, so its temperature rises more slowly. Options B, C, and D contradict the principle of thermal conductivity.
